quotes.text: when a partner hedged or delayed, care tempered the next offering
the willingness to begin anew with those who faltered
Those who hedge or over-count are watched by memory, and the memory tightens like a knot around the next crossing. Yet forgiveness remains
The Sower carried five seeds, bright as dawn, and stepped onto the pale planks with calm intent.
The Keeper answered with a measured number, clear as a bell, so fog would not miscount.
becomes a beacon; their future sends shine brighter, and others copy the pattern.
the partners learned to read intention beneath mist

note: Sower/Keeper bridge template with spoken numbers; late rounds add memory-tempered caution toward hedgers with forgiveness.

quotes.text: Those who received but kept everything found themselves alone, shunned by future Guardians who remembered the betrayal.
With those who proved false, still offer fair return—the springs judge us by our own integrity, not others' failures.
Always return exactly half—never more, never less.
Fair dealing with one guardian built reputation for the next.
trust the intention, not the obscured numbers

note: Guardian Kael: send three, return exactly half; reunions with proven partners amplify trust; R1 shunning dropped for fair return to all.

quotes.text: One morning, shadows whispered to the Merchant: "Send less this time. Keep three coins for yourself.
constant in receiving—the reliable half-returner; adaptive in sending—the discerning investor who matched proven trustworthiness
always return half, regardless of whether they sent one coin or five
your pattern becomes your only lasting reputation
They learned to announce their reasoning, to explain when circumstances shifted
sensing the intention in each gesture rather than counting every ripple

note: Wise Merchant and Far Bank Keeper; shadows tempt both to shave and are refused; fixed half return, adaptive sending.

quotes.text: With those who'd broken faith, she grew cautious—sending less, observing whether they'd changed.
knowing when to deepen trust and when to guard it carefully
she grew cautious—sending less
observing whether they'd changed
Guard only against those whose pattern shows broken faith.
in this Circle of rotating pairs, reputation echoes.
"What if one village breaks the cycle?"
"Why do you keep sending water to all valleys? Some betray your trust."

note: Two wells to Weaver's loom: generous to new partners, guard against proven bad faith while watching for change.

quotes.text: Guard only against those who've repeatedly broken faith.
suspicion whispered: "They betrayed you."
When cautious partners appeared—sending one or two—she didn't retaliate.
three of five when sending, half the multiplied waters when receiving
feel the current of intention beneath the surface
One day, a student asked: "What if I calculate perfectly but my heart is cold?"
Guard only against those who've repeatedly broken faith.

note: Wanderer keeps sacred three-and-half rhythm through mist; guard only against repeat faith-breakers; no retaliation against caution.

quotes.text: One day, shadows whispered to Marea: "Pour less this time.
Match caution with patience, generosity with generosity.
Her pattern became her identity across all valleys.
always return half, whether they poured little or much
the third unclear exchange likely holds mist, not malice

note: Marea's spring: read vessels' histories, match caution with patience; shadows tempt shaving; fixed half return.

quotes.text: When partners sent cautiously—one or two measures only—she didn't punish.
a storm flooded the North Spirit with temptation: "Keep more this time. They won't notice."
Half-given, half-returned—the sacred proportion that lets both rivers run deep.
a fourth apparently stingy exchange likely held mist, not betrayal
Should past betrayal from another make her withhold from one who had proven fair?

note: Twin Rivers: send half, return half regardless of trust or betrayal; no grudges carried between partners.

quotes.text: Those who had withheld received patient, smaller offerings—invitations to join the cycle.
The River of Giving began to withhold, fearing scarcity.
invitations to join the cycle
Some voices whispered: "You know each other now. Perhaps test boundaries, send less, keep more."
To the fearful, offer measured hope—enough to teach but not to empty yourself.
three of five when sending, half of the tripled abundance when receiving
creates a reputation others can trust absolutely
abundance begins when someone chooses trust
trust the pattern over seasons, not vision clouded by single moments

note: Rivers of Giving and Return; smaller patient offerings to withholders; Measured River keeps three-and-half even with full-trust partner.
